# Steve Eisman’s Masterclass on Financial Literacy | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 24

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman teaches long-term investing, thesis discipline, short-selling risk, valuation methods, sector behavior and interest-rate transmission. He favors simple US equity-index portfolios, insists on explicit thesis tests, and explains why short exposures grow when prices rise. His sector-based approach is practical, but several definitions and historical explanations need correction, including enterprise value, REIT cash-flow measures, the 2025 drawdown arithmetic and the claim that the Fed controls only one rate.

The most reusable contribution is the distinction between an investment thesis and the emotional reasons for continuing to hold it. Basic short-sale and discounting mathematics are sound when their assumptions are stated. Portfolio preferences are not universal suitability findings, and sector conventions are not valuation laws. The valuation primer contains material technical mistakes, so its formulas should be checked before reuse.

## Material claims

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c001"></a>
### 001. Excess leverage and mortgage exposure made the pre-2008 financial system fragile.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 3:27-4:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=207s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The FCIC documents leverage, fragile funding and mortgage-linked losses. This is a retrospective explanation, not a new forecast win.

Assessment test: Compare leverage, funding and mortgage exposures before the crisis.

- [Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13](https://fcic-static.law.stanford.edu/cdn_media/fcic-reports/fcic_final_report_full.pdf) (2011-01-27): Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c002"></a>
### 002. Post-crisis regulation forced large banks to hold more capital and made them safer.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 4:04-4:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=244s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The stress-test framework and capital buffers support improved resilience. They do not establish that all financial risk disappeared or that regulation alone explains every change.

Assessment test: Compare capital, liquidity, exposures and supervisory coverage over time.

- [2025 stress-test results, revised September 30](https://www.federalreserve.gov/publications/2025-june-dodd-frank-act-stress-test-results.htm) (2025-06-27): Aggregate CET1 13.4% at start, hypothetical trough 11.6%; institution-specific outcomes and separate leverage ratios are disclosed. Results reflect scenario, portfolio and model assumptions, not a direct measure of political intent.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c003"></a>
### 003. Another GFC-style crisis is unlikely, although a recession remains possible.

### 005. Fewer trading decisions reduce mistakes, while panic selling makes it difficult to reenter.

[Source at 5:23-6:30](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=323s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c006"></a>
### 006. If volatility becomes intolerable, first sell weak theses and trim risk instead of liquidating everything.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 6:42-7:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=402s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

He explicitly allows personal risk tolerance to override a general buy-and-hold preference. It is a decision rule, not a measurable forecast.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c007"></a>
### 007. Selling appreciated stocks can create a substantial capital-gains tax cost.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 7:49-7:58](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=469s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The conditional tax cost follows for taxable realized gains; it does not apply identically to tax-sheltered accounts or investors with offsetting losses.

Conditional reasoning: For a taxable gain G and effective tax rate t, tax cost is G × t; the rate and exemptions must be established separately.

Assessment test: Identify account type, basis, realized gain and applicable tax treatment.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c008"></a>
### 008. Most professional active managers fail to beat their benchmarks over long periods.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 8:06-8:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=486s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

SPIVA supports the broad long-horizon claim in its covered categories. It does not say that every manager or every shorter period underperforms.

Assessment test: Use survivorship-aware, after-fee results against appropriate benchmarks.

- [SPIVA US Year-End 2024](https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/spiva/article/spiva-us-year-end-2024/) (2025-03-04): No covered category had a majority of active managers outperform over the 15 years to December 2024; shorter periods differed.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c013"></a>
### 013. US equities should continue outperforming developed overseas markets over the long term.

**Too early** | Steve Eisman | forecast | major

[Source at 11:12-11:38](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=672s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: long term, no exact end date

The preference for US dynamism becomes a long-term relative-return thesis, but no completed long-term horizon or precise benchmark is supplied.

Assessment test: Define US and ex-US total-return benchmarks, currency treatment and a prospective horizon.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c014"></a>
### 014. A foreign stock gain can be offset by a currency loss for a US investor.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 11:38-11:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=698s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The currency translation mechanism is correct; whether to hedge is a separate portfolio choice.

Conditional reasoning: USD return = (1 + local return) × (1 + currency return) - 1. A 10% local gain and 10% currency fall produce -1%.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 17:00-18:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1020s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c023"></a>
### 023. If a $4,000 position halves while the total portfolio remains $100,000, its weight falls from 4% to 2%.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 18:57-20:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1137s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The example correctly measures position exposure under its explicit constant-total-portfolio assumption; it does not prove lower business risk.

Conditional reasoning: 2,000 / 100,000 = 2%; the remaining 98,000 / 24 positions is about 4,083.33 each.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c024"></a>
### 024. Short selling borrows shares, sells them, then buys them back for return; a lower repurchase price produces a gross gain.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 20:13-21:03](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1213s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The basic mechanics are correct. Borrow expense and other obligations reduce gross profit.

Assessment test: Reconcile sale proceeds, repurchase price, borrowing charges and distributions.

- [Short Selling: Background and Policy Issues](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/IF/PDF/IF12400/IF12400.2.pdf) (2023-05-12): A short sale borrows shares for later return; losses can be unlimited as the repurchase price rises.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c025"></a>
### 025. Borrowing is usually arranged through the desk, but illiquid or heavily shorted stocks can cost 20%-30% a year or more.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 21:08-21:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1268s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The friction is material, but no dated loan quote is supplied to verify the cited fee range for a particular trade. Borrow availability is not guaranteed.

Assessment test: Inspect the actual locate, loan agreement, variable fee and recall terms.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c026"></a>
### 026. Buying by shorts covering a rising illiquid stock can amplify a short squeeze.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 21:52-22:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1312s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a conditional feedback mechanism, not a forecast that every crowded short must squeeze.

Conditional reasoning: If forced covering adds purchase demand while available sell supply is limited, the clearing price must adjust until supply meets demand.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c027"></a>
### 027. A short initially equal to 4% of the portfolio becomes an 8% position when its stock doubles.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 22:58-23:06](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1378s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Gross short liability doubles, but the equity denominator also falls from the loss unless other gains offset it. With no offset, exposure becomes about 8.33%.

Conditional reasoning: Start with equity 100 and short liability 4. A doubling creates liability 8 and loss 4, leaving equity 96; 8 / 96 = 8.33%. The stated 8% requires equity to stay 100.

Assessment test: Separate gross liability from net portfolio equity.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c028"></a>
### 028. An unhedged short has theoretically unlimited loss, and rising exposure can force risk managers to cover.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 23:06-23:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1386s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Unlimited price risk is mathematically correct. A particular forced-cover threshold depends on margin, borrowing and internal risk limits.

Conditional reasoning: For fixed shares N, short profit before costs is N × (sale price - repurchase price); there is no fixed upper bound on the latter.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c029"></a>
### 029. Valuation matters over the long term, but an expensive stock with intact fundamentals is a dangerous short solely on valuation.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 24:19-25:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1459s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This distinguishes a valuation concern from a catalyst and is a risk-management rule, not a claim that price never matters.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c030"></a>
### 030. The internet bubble broke because recession damaged earnings, rather than because valuation changed.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 25:23-25:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1523s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The recession began in 2001, after the 2000 technology-market peak. Later recession damage cannot explain the chronology as stated or establish that valuation had no role.

Assessment test: Distinguish the beginning of the market collapse from later earnings deterioration.

- [March 2001 business-cycle peak](https://www.nber.org/news/business-cycle-dating-committee-announcement-november-26-2001) (2001-11-26): The recession began after the March 2001 business-cycle peak, about a year after the Nasdaq March 2000 peak.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c031"></a>
### 031. Nvidia’s 2023 earnings revisions made a previously expensive-looking stock retrospectively inexpensive.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 25:55-26:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1555s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Rapid earnings growth can compress a forward multiple, but the claim needs dated prices and contemporaneous consensus revisions. Hindsight earnings do not prove the original price was low-risk.

Assessment test: Reconstruct the original forward estimate and subsequent revisions without look-ahead.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c032"></a>
### 032. Market capitalization equals share price multiplied by shares outstanding.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 27:01-27:13](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1621s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is the standard equity-value identity; the approximate Apple value is an illustrative, date-sensitive input.

Conditional reasoning: Equity market value = price per share × shares outstanding.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c033"></a>
### 033. Enterprise value equals equity market capitalization plus debt.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 27:13-27:22](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1633s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

That omits cash and other relevant adjustments. It is not a generally correct operating-enterprise-value formula, particularly for cash-rich companies.

Assessment test: Reconcile equity, debt, excess cash, minority interests and other claims consistently.

- [Financial ratios and measures: enterprise value](https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/definitions.html) (inspected 2026-11-10): Operating enterprise value nets cash from equity plus debt and adds minority interests where appropriate; debt plus equity alone includes non-operating cash.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c034"></a>
### 034. P/E is share price divided by earnings per share; forward P/E substitutes a forecast EPS.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 27:22-27:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1642s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The ratio identity is correct. The reliability of a forward multiple depends on the earnings definition and forecast.

Conditional reasoning: P/E = share price / EPS for a specified period and accounting basis.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c035"></a>
### 035. June 18, 2025 forward multiples differ widely: Nvidia 34, Goldman 14, P&G 23, Lilly 36, Lennar 11, Exxon 18 and Eaton 28.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 27:55-28:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1675s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

These are dated consensus examples, not current valuations. The original consensus vendor and exact forecast basis were not inspected.

Assessment test: Match each June 18 close to the same-date 2025 EPS consensus and fiscal-year basis.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c036"></a>
### 036. Growth, earnings cyclicality, leverage and stability help explain differing sector P/E ratios.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 28:32-29:56](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1712s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The proposed determinants are plausible but do not uniquely identify the observed cross-section; multiple factors can move together.

### 037. Sector-allocation mandates force funds into consumer staples and raise P&G’s multiple despite slow EPS growth.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

No mandate sample or flow-based valuation attribution is supplied. Some funds have tight sector limits; this does not establish the stated dominant explanation.

### 039. He avoids long-term oil-stock investment because forecasting oil prices is too difficult.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 31:53-32:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1913s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c040"></a>
### 040. Eaton deserves a growth multiple from reindustrialization, and Lilly’s multiple reflects profits expected from its drug pipeline.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 32:02-32:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1922s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

These are valuation narratives. The specific high-teens growth and future drug-profit assumptions need matched disclosures and a cash-flow model.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c041"></a>
### 041. EBITDA adds interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization back to net earnings.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 32:41-33:10](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1961s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The unadjusted reconciliation is correct; company-defined adjusted EBITDA may add further items.

Conditional reasoning: EBITDA = net income + interest expense + tax expense + depreciation + amortization, with consistent scope.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c042"></a>
### 042. EBITDA per share is always greater than EPS.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 33:12-33:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=1992s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Usually positive add-backs make it larger, but the word always fails when net interest or tax benefits outweigh depreciation and other additions.

Conditional reasoning: If net income is 100, tax expense is -30 and total remaining add-backs are 10, EBITDA is 80, below net income. Dividing both by the same share count preserves the inequality.

Assessment test: Inspect signs and definitions rather than assume every add-back is positive.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c043"></a>
### 043. John Malone pioneered EBITDA to show the cash-generating potential of debt-funded telecom expansion.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 33:27-34:32](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2007s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The origin and personal rationale are historical assertions without an inspected contemporaneous source here. EBITDA is not itself cash available after investment.

Assessment test: Check contemporary Malone statements and reconcile cash flow, capex and borrowing.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c044"></a>
### 044. EBITDA can give a misleading economic picture by excluding the cost of maintaining capital-intensive assets.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 34:32-35:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2072s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The limitation follows from the metric. This supports a measurement warning, not a verdict on every company valued using EBITDA.

Conditional reasoning: Adding depreciation back and omitting capital expenditure leaves replacement investment outside EBITDA; identical EBITDA can coexist with very different free cash flow.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c045"></a>
### 045. Book value per share uses common equity per share; tangible book removes goodwill and other intangibles.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 35:20-35:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2120s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The accounting bridge is correct when common equity, other intangible assets and share counts are defined consistently.

Conditional reasoning: Tangible common equity per share = (common equity - goodwill - other applicable intangibles) / common shares.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c046"></a>
### 046. Hidden asset losses make balance-sheet reliability central to bank valuation.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 35:42-36:11](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2142s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The financial-crisis evidence supports the importance of unrecognized losses and funding exposures. Tangible book is still an accounting estimate, not a guaranteed liquidation value.

Assessment test: Inspect asset marks, loss allowances, capital and off-balance-sheet exposures.

- [Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13](https://fcic-static.law.stanford.edu/cdn_media/fcic-reports/fcic_final_report_full.pdf) (2011-01-27): Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c047"></a>
### 047. JPMorgan trades around 2.4 times tangible book and Citi around 0.7 because JPMorgan earns higher returns.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 36:15-36:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2175s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The prices and return measures are date-sensitive, and ROE must not be confused with ROTCE. No matched snapshot establishes these exact multiples or the complete causal explanation.

Assessment test: Use the same date and denominator for market value, tangible equity and profitability.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c048"></a>
### 048. DCF values a business by discounting expected future cash flows to present value.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 36:39-37:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2199s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is the valuation identity, not a claim that distant forecasts can be known precisely.

Conditional reasoning: Present value = sum over t of expected cash flow at t divided by (1 + discount rate)^t, plus any consistently defined terminal value.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c049"></a>
### 049. He prefers researching business fundamentals to building precise decades-long DCF forecasts.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 37:30-38:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2250s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is an explicit methodological preference. DCF sensitivity is a reason to use scenarios, not a mathematical invalidation of discounting.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c050"></a>
### 050. Sector specialists collectively determine the metrics and valuation conventions that markets use for long periods.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 38:15-40:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2295s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The account describes professional practice, but consensus, its persistence and its price-setting power are not measured. It does not make an established convention economically correct.

Assessment test: Track sector research methods and prices across time, including competing valuation approaches.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c051"></a>
### 051. Choose valuation tools by business model: P/E for many sectors, tangible book for banks, reserves for oil, pipeline economics for drugs and sometimes DCF for unprofitable growth.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 40:40-42:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2440s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a practical classification heuristic. These are overlapping tools, not exclusive rules, and cash-flow consistency still matters.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c052"></a>
### 052. REIT FFO is a cash-flow measure calculated from pretax earnings, adding depreciation and subtracting property gains and interest income.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 42:17-43:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2537s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The stated bridge conflates FFO with other measures. Nareit FFO begins with GAAP net income, and is expressly not GAAP operating cash flow; interest income is not a universal FFO subtraction.

Assessment test: Use the issuer’s reconciliation to the Nareit definition and distinguish cash-flow statements.

- [2025 supplemental definitions: FFO and FAD](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1500217/000150021726000004/a4q25supplemental.htm) (2026): Nareit FFO starts with GAAP net income, adjusts real-estate depreciation and sale gains/losses, and is not GAAP operating cash flow. The FAD reconciliation deducts recurring capital and leasing costs.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c053"></a>
### 053. AFFO adds back capital expenditures and then deducts maintenance capex as a standard REIT valuation formula.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 43:01-43:17](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2581s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

AFFO is not standardized. Recurring capex is commonly deducted from FFO-based measures; capital spending is not generally an expense already removed from FFO that can simply be added back.

Assessment test: Inspect the individual issuer’s AFFO bridge and avoid double-counting capex.

- [Q2 2026 definitions: AFFO](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364250/000136425026000038/a2026q2epexhibit991.htm) (2026): AFFO deducts recurring capital expenditures and leasing costs from adjusted FFO. Nareit has not standardized AFFO, so company definitions differ.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c054"></a>
### 054. Utilities are often assessed with earnings multiples and dividend yields.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 43:19-43:25](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2599s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

These are valuation inputs, not an outcome prediction; financing, regulation and investment requirements remain necessary context.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c055"></a>
### 055. After the financial crisis, tangible book displaced ordinary book value so completely that only tangible book is used for banks.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 43:25-44:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2605s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The preference for tangible equity is understandable, but the exclusive claim is not established by an exhaustive survey. His own discussion also uses earnings and returns.

Assessment test: Inspect bank research and transaction valuations across book, tangible book, earnings and cash-flow approaches.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c056"></a>
### 056. Growth, cyclical and defensive sector labels are useful simplifications but can hide large differences among subsectors.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 44:40-46:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2680s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

He explicitly warns against treating the labels as universal. A defensive business can still have an expensive or risky stock.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c057"></a>
### 057. A drop in the S&P 500 from 6,144 to 4,983 is a 16% decline.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 46:41-47:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2801s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The stated levels imply an approximately 18.9% decline. This correction uses his own numbers and does not require an assumed chart series.

Conditional reasoning: 4,983 / 6,144 - 1 = -18.8965%, not -16%.

Assessment test: Calculate point-to-point return using the starting level as denominator.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c058"></a>
### 058. The rebound from about 4,983 to 5,985 is approximately 20%.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 47:15-47:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2835s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

That percentage is arithmetically correct for those supplied levels. The date labels and exact quoted closing levels remain separate verification questions.

Conditional reasoning: 5,985 / 4,983 - 1 = 20.1084%.

Assessment test: Verify the chosen endpoints and whether the return window begins at the April 8 close.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c059"></a>
### 059. Defensive sectors fell less during the selloff, while technology and cyclicals rebounded more strongly; healthcare lagged the rebound.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 47:42-49:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2862s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The pattern is stated through a table, but the exact sector-return series, total-return basis and endpoints were not independently inspected.

Assessment test: Recalculate all eleven sector indexes for identical starting and ending closes.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c060"></a>
### 060. A 20% gain does not recover a preceding 20% loss.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 48:44-48:54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2924s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The compounding correction is correct.

Conditional reasoning: Starting at 100, a 20% fall leaves 80; a 20% rise then leaves 96. Recovery requires a 25% gain.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c061"></a>
### 061. Defensive sectors can still lose money in a correction even while outperforming other sectors.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 49:04-49:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2944s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is the correct distinction between relative defensiveness and absolute capital protection; the specific sample returns remain separately unresolved.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c062"></a>
### 062. Healthcare missed the rally because Trump made Medicare and Medicaid pay the lowest foreign drug price.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 49:50-50:09](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=2990s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A most-favored-nation initiative was announced, but the order directs targets and possible later rulemaking rather than an immediate universal price substitution. It also does not establish the entire sector’s causal return attribution.

Assessment test: Distinguish announcement, binding implementation, affected products and event-study evidence.

- [Most-favored-nation drug-pricing executive order](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/05/delivering-most-favored-nation-prescription-drug-pricing-to-american-patients/) (2025-05-12): The order directs price targets and possible later rulemaking if progress is inadequate. It does not instantly replace every Medicare and Medicaid drug price with the lowest foreign price.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c063"></a>
### 063. June sector weights show technology dominates the US index and explain why a tech bull should prefer US equities to Europe.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 50:11-52:05](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3011s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The stated weights are not fully consistent across later passages, and the investment conclusion needs valuation and overlap analysis as well as sector share.

Assessment test: Reconstruct the same-date weights and compare broad economic exposures under consistent definitions.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c064"></a>
### 064. Within sectors, payments and biotech can be growth businesses while traditional banks are cyclical and staples are relatively defensive.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 52:05-57:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3125s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The useful lesson is to classify by economics rather than the sector label alone. These are broad conventions with many exceptions, not forecasts for every constituent.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c065"></a>
### 065. Cord cutting and streaming have damaged the former defensive character of traditional media and cable.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 55:36-55:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3336s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The mechanism is plausible, but company-specific cash flow, subscriber trends and valuations determine how much value is impaired.

Assessment test: Separate linear-video decline from broadband, connectivity and other segment economics.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c066"></a>
### 066. Celebrity brands and influencers have intensified beauty competition and hurt established companies.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 57:06-57:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3426s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The industry-change thesis lacks a matched market-share and profit attribution study here.

Assessment test: Compare brand shares, marketing costs and incumbent margins over the specified period.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c067"></a>
### 067. Solar is the principal growth exception within the S&P Energy sector.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 57:38-57:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3458s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The discussion confuses an energy-related economic activity with index classification. GICS places solar-module and cell manufacturers in Information Technology, with renewable electricity elsewhere.

Assessment test: Use official GICS categories when explaining S&P sector weights.

- [GICS methodology, Information Technology definitions](https://www.msci.com/documents/1296102/11185224/GICS%2BMethodology%2B2022.pdf) (2022-01): The Information Technology semiconductor category includes manufacturers of solar modules and cells. Solar is not simply a subsector of the GICS Energy sector.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c068"></a>
### 068. Higher financing costs and adverse federal policy weakened residential solar demand and stocks.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 58:19-58:57](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3499s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The proposed channels are plausible, but this passage does not isolate them from pricing, inventories, state policy or company execution. The $30,000 system price is illustrative.

Assessment test: Compare financed monthly payments, installations and company-specific demand alongside policy changes.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c069"></a>
### 069. Office REITs lost their former defensive character as office-property values declined.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 58:57-59:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3537s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The broad diagnosis needs dated, property-specific evidence; it does not establish that the downturn is over or that every REIT has the same exposure.

Assessment test: Inspect vacancies, leases, valuations, debt maturities and actual asset sales.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c070"></a>
### 070. Regulated utilities have relatively predictable profits and defensive characteristics.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 59:20-59:43](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3560s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

Regulation can improve visibility, but allowed returns, cost recovery, debt financing and exceptional liabilities prevent guaranteed profitability.

Assessment test: Inspect rate cases, capital plans, recovery mechanisms and financing needs.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c071"></a>
### 071. The Fed controls only the federal funds rate and no other interest rate.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:00:13-1:00:41](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3613s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

It directly administers reserve-interest, reverse-repo and discount rates as well. The useful distinction is between policy instruments and market-determined longer-term yields, not that the Fed sets only one rate.

Assessment test: Distinguish administered rates, the funds target and the effective market rate.

- [Ample-reserves monetary-policy implementation](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/implementing-monetary-policy-in-an-ample-reserves-regime-the-basics-note-1-of-3-20200701.html) (2020-07-01): The Fed sets administered reserve-interest and reverse-repo rates to guide the federal funds market rate. The discount rate is also administered; long-term yields are not directly fixed by the funds target.

<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c072"></a>
### 072. Long rates usually exceed short rates because lending for longer is riskier.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:00:41-1:01:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3641s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A term premium can contribute, but expected future short rates and changing risk premia also determine the curve. No historical frequency or exclusive causal decomposition is established.

Assessment test: Decompose yields into expected policy rates and term premia.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c073"></a>
### 073. For fixed promised bond cash flows, a higher price implies a lower yield.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:01:04-1:01:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3664s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The inverse relationship is correct when cash flows and maturity are held constant.

Conditional reasoning: Bond price is the sum of fixed positive cash flows discounted at yield; increasing yield reduces each present value.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c074"></a>
### 074. Fear of recession can pull long yields below short yields, but inversion does not perfectly predict recession.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:01:32-1:02:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3692s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is a qualified interpretation rather than a deterministic signal. The passage supplies no specified spread, lead time or false-positive study.

Assessment test: Compare a defined spread and lead window with an official recession chronology.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c075"></a>
### 075. A steeper yield curve increases bank net interest margins because banks fund short and lend long.

**Mixed** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:02:08-1:03:04](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3728s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The stylized maturity transformation is useful, but the implication is not automatic: deposit betas, asset repricing, hedges, funding mix and credit losses can offset it.

Conditional reasoning: Suppose the market short rate is unchanged and the long rate rises 1 point, steepening the curve. If a bank raises previously low deposit rates by 2 points to retain funding while asset yield rises 1 point, its spread falls 1 point. The claimed result requires assumptions about deposit pricing and asset repricing.

Assessment test: Model asset and liability repricing rather than use slope alone.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c076"></a>
### 076. Rising long-term rates need not hurt stocks when they reflect stronger growth without excessive inflation.

**Not testable** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 1:03:06-1:03:26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3786s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

He qualifies the usual inverse-rate heuristic. The net outcome depends on earnings revisions and discount rates, so this is a scenario framework.

Assessment test: Use as a decision rule, not a dated return forecast.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c077"></a>
### 077. Inflation-driven Fed tightening caused the 2022 equity decline, although the feared recession did not occur.

**Unresolved** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:03:29-1:04:19](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3809s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The rate and earnings-risk channels are plausible, but the attribution is not isolated. The cited roughly 18% decline requires a total-return rather than price-only definition.

Assessment test: Separate price and total returns, realized recession dates and the contribution of earnings versus discount rates.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c078"></a>
### 078. With projected positive cash flows fixed, increasing the discount rate reduces DCF value.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:04:21-1:05:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3861s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

This is correct conditional mathematics. Actual market moves also change growth forecasts and risk premia.

Conditional reasoning: For each positive future cash flow C at time t, C/(1+r)^t declines as r rises; summing preserves the direction.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


<a id="youtube-u8chA7LC8lU-c079"></a>
### 079. Cash flows concentrated farther in the future are more sensitive to discount-rate changes than equally valued nearer cash flows.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 1:05:23-1:06:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u8chA7LC8lU&t=3923s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The duration mechanism is correct; it does not guarantee that every growth stock underperforms every staple whenever rates rise.

Conditional reasoning: The proportional sensitivity of a single discounted cash flow is -t/(1+r); later t means larger sensitivity at the same rate.

Assessment test: Check the stated assumptions and calculation.


## Framework and tools

- Write the investment thesis and the observable facts that would disprove it before becoming attached to the stock.
- Distinguish business deterioration, valuation and the funding constraints that can force a short seller to cover.
- Learn the metrics used by sector specialists, but reconcile them to cash generation and the balance sheet.
- Separate a defensive business from a stock guaranteed to avoid losses.
- He distrusts decades-long DCF precision and prefers nearer-term business fundamentals.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Forward P/E and dated consensus estimates.
- Enterprise value / EBITDA, price / tangible book, DCF and REIT FFO/AFFO.
- Position weights, borrow costs, short interest and short-squeeze mechanics.
- Sector weights and relative returns during the February-May 2025 selloff and rebound.
- Yield curve, net interest margin and discount-rate sensitivity.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.
- Read all 1,502 caption segments through the closing disclosure.
- Many examples explicitly use June 18, 2025 prices and consensus estimates despite the September 8 listing date; they are not September spot valuations.
- Captions corrupt EBITDA, AFFO, company names and some numbers. The drawdown correction uses the stated index levels, so it does not depend on an assumed transcription of an unviewed table.
- The sector-weight discussion gives inconsistent rounded weights in different passages; the displayed tables were not independently inspected.
